BASE PROSPECTUS   
 
 
 
COMPASS GROUP PLC 
(incorporated with limited liability in England and Wales under registered number 4083914) 
£6,000,000,000 Euro Medium Term Note Programme 
 
Compass Group PLC ( the "Issuer") has established a Euro Medium Term Note Programme (the "Programme") described in this Base Prospectus  under which 
notes ("Notes") may be issued.  
This Base Prospectus has been approved by the United Kingdom Financial Conduct Authority (the "FCA"), as competent authority under Regulation (EU) 
2017/1129 as it forms part of domestic law in the United Kingdom ("UK") by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018, as amended ("EUWA") (the 
"UK Prospectus Regulation "). The FCA only approves this Base Prospectus as meeting the standards of completeness, comprehensibility and consistency 
imposed by the UK Prospectus Regulation. Such approval should not be considered as an endorsement of the Issuer or as an endo rsement of the quality of any 
Notes that are the subject of this Base Prospectus. Investors should make their own assessment as to the suitability of inves ting in such Notes.  
Application has been made for the Notes (other than the Exempt Notes (as defined below)) to be admitted during the period of 12 months after the date hereof to 
listing on the Official List of the FCA and to trading within the period of 12 months from the date of this Base Prospectus on the Main Market of the London Stock 
Exchange plc (the "Main Market"). This Base Prospectus (as supplemented from time to time) is valid for a period of 12 months from the date of approval. 
The requirement to publish a prospectus under the UK Prospectus Regulation only applies to Notes which are to be admitted to trading on a regulated market in 
the United Kingdom and/or offered to the public in the United Kingdom other than in circumstances where an exemption is available under Article 1(4) and/or 
3(2) of the UK Prospectus Regulation. References in this Base Prospectus to "Exempt Notes" are to Notes issued under the Programme for which no prospectus 
is required to be published under the UK Prospectus Regulation or under the United Kingdom Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, as amended . The FCA 
has neither approved nor reviewed information contained in this Base Prospectus in connection with Exempt Notes.  The applicable pricing supplement (the 
"Pricing Supplement") in respect of the issue of any Exempt Notes will specify whether or not such Exempt Notes will be admitted to listing or tr ading on any 
stock exchanges and/or markets, if applicable. 
Investing in Notes issued under the Programme involves certain risks. The principal risk factors that may affect the abilities of the Issuer to fulfil its obligations 
under the Notes are discussed under "Risk Factors" below. 
The Notes have not been, nor will they be, registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act") or with any securities 
regulatory authority of any state or other jurisdiction of the United States, and Notes in bearer form are subject to U.S. tax law requirements. The Notes may not 
be offered, sold or (in the case of Notes in bearer form) delivered within the United States or to, or for the account or ben efit of, U.S. persons (as defined in 
Regulation S under the Securities Act ("Regulation S")) except in certain transactions exempt from the registration requirements of the Securities Act.  
The Issuer has been assigned a rating of A by S&P Global Ratings UK Limited  ("Standard and Poor's") and a rating of A 2 by Moody's Investors Service Ltd . 
("Moody's"). Each of Standard and Poor 's and Moody 's is a credit rating agency established and operating in the UK and registered under Regulation (EU) No 
1060/2009 as it forms part of domestic law of the UK by virtue of the EUWA  (the "UK CRA Regulation"). Each of Standard and Poor 's and Moody's appears 
on the latest update of the list of registered credit rating agencies (as of 12 June 2025) on the UK FCA's Financial Services Register. The ratings each of Standard 
and Poor's and Moody 's have given to  the Issuer are endorsed by S&P Global Ratings Europe Limited and Moody's Deutschland GmbH  respectively, both of 
which are established in the European Economic Area ("EEA") and registered under Regulation (EU) No 1060/2009, as amended (the "EU CRA Regulation"). 
Tranches of Notes issued under the Programme may be rated or unrated. Where a Tranche of Notes is rated, such rating(s) will not necessarily be the same as the 
ratings described above or the rating(s) assigned to Notes already issued. The rating(s) assigned to a particular Tranche of Notes issued under the Programme will 
be disclosed in the Final Terms. A rating is not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold Notes and ma y be subject to suspension, change or withdrawal at any time 
by the assigning rating agency.

CITIGROUP

IMPORTANT NOTICES 
This Base Prospectus (together with any supplementary prospectus and any documents incorporated by 
reference, the "Base Prospectus") contains summary information provided by the Issuer in connection with 
the Programme under which the Issuer may issue and have outstanding at any time Notes up to a maximum 
aggregate amount (together with Notes historically issued by Compass Group Finance Netherlands B.V. 
under the Programme) of £6,000,000,000 or its equivalent in alternative currencies. Under the Programme, 
the Issuer may issue Notes outside the United States pursuant to Regulation S. The Issuer has, pursuant to 
an amended and restated dealer agreement dated 13 June 2025  (the "Dealer Agreement "), appointed 
Citigroup Global Markets Limited as a dealer for the Notes (together with any dealers for the day, the 
"Dealers"), and authorised and requested the Dealers to circulate the Base Prospectus in connection with 
the Programme on their behalf to purchasers or potential purchasers of the Notes.

(as defined below) for each Tranche (as defined herein) of Notes issued under the Programme and declares

in accordance with the facts and the Base Prospectus makes no omission likely to affect its import.  
Each Tranche (as defined herein) of Notes will be issued on the terms set out herein under "Terms and

subject of a Pricing Supplement or a Drawdown Prospectus, each reference in this Base Prospectus to 
information being specified or identified in the relevant Final Terms shall be read and construed as a

particular, each potential investor should: 
(i) have sufficient knowledge and experience to make a meaningful evaluation of the Notes, the merits 
and risks of investing in the Notes and the information contained or incorporated by reference in 
this Base Prospectus or any applicable supplement; 
(ii) have access to, and knowledge of, appropriate analytical tools to evaluate, in the context of its

(iii) have sufficient financial resources and liquidity to bear all of the risks of an investment in the Notes, 
including Notes with principal or interest payable in one or more currencies, or where the currency 
for principal or interest payments is different from the potential investor's currency; 
(iv) understand thoroughly the terms of the Notes and be familiar with the behaviour of any relevant 
indices and financial markets; and 
(v) be able to evaluate (either alone or with the help of a financial adviser) possible scenarios for

applicable risks.

investment will have on the potential investor's overall investment portfolio.

causing operational disruptions and adverse financial, legal, and reputational consequences to  the Group.

affect the Group’s business, financial condition, operations and the results of operations.

key to the long-term success of the Group. Changes to economic conditions may increase the risk of attrition 
at all levels of the organisation. The Group’s business, financial condition , operations and the results of 
operations may be adversely affected if the Group ’s businesses are not able to attract, retain and motivate

Financial Management Risks 
Credit Risk 
At any one point in time the Group will hold a significant level of trade receivables and is therefore exposed 
to the risk that it may not be able to collect the full value of its trade receivables if the creditworthiness of 
its individual clients was to deteriorate. The Group’s overall credit risk is limited as a result of the diverse 
and unrelated nature of its client base. However, an economic downturn could affect the solvency of clients 
and adversely affect the Group’s business, financial condition and the results of operations. 
Currency Fluctuations 
The Group’s subsidiaries and associated companies operate in a number of countries and will generally buy 
and sell goods and services in their local currencies. However, on consolidation the local currency results 
and closing balance sheets will be translated into US dollars, which, from 1 October 2023, is the Issuer’s 
reporting currency. Prior to this date the Issuer’s reporting currency was Sterling. The Issuer is only partially 
protected from the impact of exchange rate fluctuations through the matching of cash flows to currency 
borrowings. The Issuer’s consolidated financial statements will therefore be affected (either positively or 
negatively) by fluctuations in the currencies of its underlying businesses. 
While the Issuer implements currency hedging policies, the US dollar value of both its net debt and 
operating profits may fluctuate as exchange rates vary. 
Liquidity Risk 
The Group raises finance in both the public markets and the US private placement market and therefore 
depends on access to investors in these capital markets. The Group also uses committed and uncommitted 
bank loans, other lines of credit and commercial paper to cover its liquidity needs. Global events have, from 
time to time, resulted in the closure of the debt capital markets and a reduced capacity within the bank and 
private placement market to provide credit lines or loans. Whilst the Group has successf ully raised funds 
in the equity markets in the past and would expect to be able to do so again, there can be no assurance that 
it will be able to continue to do so. 
Reduced appetite for the Group ’s debt instruments in such markets could limit the ability of the Group to 
fund operations and therefore adversely affect the Group’s business and financial condition. 
Interest Rate Risk 
The Group ’s debt service costs are subject to variations in the underlying interest rates. Central banks 
including the Federal Reserve in the US, the Bank of England and the European Central Bank continue to 
take steps to manage interest rates and inflation. In order to mitigate the impact of interest rate fluctuation, 
the Issuer’s policy is to fix the interest rates on its principal debt currencies so that, in the short term, it is 
not materially exposed to changes in interest rates. Sustained long -term increases in interest rates could 
adversely affect the financial condition and operating results of the Issuer.  
Reliance upon dividend and interest income and/or loans in order to satisfy payment obligations under the 
Notes. 
The Issuer is a non-trading investment holding company  and is the parent company  of the Group. As a 
result, the assets of the Issuer consist principally of its shareholdings in and loans to other companies in the 
Group. The ability of the Issuer to satisfy payment obligations under the Notes is dependent upon its receipt 
of dividend and interest payments from other members of the Group. In circumstances where one or more 
of the risks referred to herein arises and adversely affects the business, financial con dition, operations or 
operational results of any member of the Group there may in turn be an adverse effect on the ability of that 
member of the Group to make dividend and/or interest payments to the Issuer, so as to enable the Issuer to 
satisfy its payment obligations under the Notes. 
Acquisitions and Investments 
The Group may acquire businesses and it makes capital investments. Difficulties in integrating acquired 
businesses, or realising the expected synergies or benefits of capital investment, may have an adverse effect 
on the Group’s business, financial condition, operations and results of operations.

DESCRIPTION OF THE ISSUER 
General 
The Issuer is the holding company of the Group (being the Issuer and its subsidiaries from time to time), a 
global leader in food services  operating in around 30  countries in North America, Europe and Asia 
Pacific, with annual underlying revenue of U.S.$42.2 billion (in the financial year ended 30 September 
2024).  
The Issuer was incorporated on 29 September 2000 in the United Kingdom and operates under English 
law. It was initially registered under the name of Compass Demerger Limited prior to changing its name 
to Compass  Group PLC and re-registering as a public limited company (with the registered number 
04083914) under the Companies Act 1985 on 30 November 2000. The Issuer was listed on the London 
Stock Exchange on 2 February 2001. 
The registered office of the Issuer is Compass House, Guildford Street, Chertsey,  Surrey KT16 9BQ. 
The telephone number of the Issuer's registered office is +44 (0)1932 573 000. 
Business Overview 
The Group’s core focus is the provision of outsourced food services and targeted support services to five 
key market sectors. The Group aims to create bespoke, innovative and cost effective solutions through 
its unique sectorised approach to the market. By understanding what is important to its clients, the Group 
seeks to address  their unique needs and create long -lasting partnerships.  The Group operates on a 
decentralised basis, enabling an entrepreneurial approach by local country management teams.  
Management believes that the Group has a strong financial foundation with a low level of leverage 
which means the Group can invest in growth, enabling its businesses to innovate their offer, and evolve 
their operating model. Management consider that the Group’s financial strength also attracts new clients 
seeking stability and long -term outsourcing solutions  and that the Group’s scale enables its businesses to 
pass on purchasing benefits to clients and consumers by offering quality products at more attractive prices. 
Management also consider that purchasing from local and diverse suppliers and social enterprises enables 
greater reinvestment into local communities. The Group has targeted climate net zero greenhouse gas 
emissions by 2050 alongside validated science-based targets to reduce emissions by 2030 (from a 2019 
base year) in line with the Paris Agreement and has made reducing food waste a Group priority. 
The Group prioritises investment in capital expenditure to support organic growth in both new business 
wins and retention of existing contracts, and bolt-on M&A opportunities that strengthen its capabilities 
and broaden its exposure.  
People, Performance and Purpose 
The Group endeavours to manage its business with a disciplined focus on People, Performance and 
Purpose as its main strategic priorities. The People pillar is focused on ensuring the Group creates 
opportunities for its employees and positively impacts and represents the communities in which it 
operates. The Performance pillar is focused on delivering long-term valued relationships. The Group 
drives operational efficiency via the Management and Performance ("MAP") framework (see further 
below), while continuing to focus on delivering innovative, healthy and exciting food service solutions 
for clients and consumers. The Purpose pillar addresses the Group's social and environmental 
responsibilities. The Group  continually aims to seek ways to be more socially and environmentally 
responsible.  
Market sectors 
The Group segments its markets into the following five sectors: Business & Industry ; Education; 
Healthcare & Senior Living; Sports & Leisure; and Defence, Offshore & Remote. The Group considers 
that its  sector and sub -sector portfolio enables the operating businesses to focus on the different 
requirements of and to create bespoke solutions for its clients:

89   
Business & Industry 
In this sector the Group works with a diverse range of clients including in the financial, legal, technology 
and manufacturing sectors. The Group’s scale, flexible operating models and digital capabilities help it 
to tailor its dining solutions to each client. 
In addition, the Group can deliver a range of hospitality-led services. 
Sector brands include: Eurest, Restaurant Associates, Bon Appétit, Flik, Canteen and ESFM.  
Healthcare & Senior Living 
In this sector the Group works directly with healthcare providers and aims to prepare food that improves 
patient and senior living experiences – from restaurant -style cafés to in -room patient dining and 
specialist feeding. The Group also provides a range of bespoke support services such as  patient 
transportation and laundry and linen services. 
Sector brands include: Medirest, Crothall, Morrison and Unidine.  
Education 
Within the Education sector the Group provides healthy, balanced meals right through the learning 
journey, from nurseries to universities. The Group’s catering solutions come in multiple formats, from 
traditional onsite dining to vending and delivery or takeaway options. 
The Group can also provide tailored support service packages along with the dining solutions such as 
cleaning and waste management. 
Sector brands include: Chartwells, Bon Appétit, SSC and Flik.  
Sports & Leisure 
The Group aims to enhance  customer experiences, providing food, beverages and hospitality across 
large stadiums, conference venues, museums and galleries. 
Sector brands include: Levy and Restaurant Associates. 
Defence, Offshore & Remote 
In the remote and offshore sector, the Group provides food and support services to many major oil, gas, 
mining and construction companies. The Group aims  to provide uninterrupted support, however 
challenging the operating conditions. 
In the defence sector, the Group targets operations outside of areas of conflict. 
Sector brand: ESS Support Services Worldwide. 
Consumer brands 
The Group maintains and develops its portfolio of consumer -facing brands which have been acquired 
and scaled over time. To complement the Group's in-house brands in certain markets and countries, the 
Group leverages  its scale to operate major "high-street" consumer brands from its  clients' premises. 
These are normally operated on a franchise basis, which enables the Group to combine its market 
expertise and service skills with the consumer awareness of such brands. 
Clients 
As noted above, the Group has a diverse sector portfolio, and a wide ranging client base. 
Contracts with clients are  principally based on a cost -plus, profit and loss or fixed price model. Input 
cost increases are mitigated wherever possible with some pricing passed on to clients under the various 
contract structures. The cost -plus model is the easiest to pass through price followed by the profit and 
loss model which enables the Group to change consumer  prices subject to competitive pressure. Cost

90   
increases under the fixed price contracts are typically linked to contractual indexation clauses which are 
reviewed at various intervals as specified in the client terms. 
Geographical Diversification 
The Group has a geographically and culturally diverse business with operations in around 30 countries in 
North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. 
The Group's  operations are managed on a  country-by-country basis . Until 30 September 2024, the 
Group reported performance through three regions: North America; Europe and Rest of World. Based

Management and Performance framework 
The Group uses its MAP framework to drive performance across the business. MAP is a simple 
framework which is embedded in the Group's culture and allows it to ensure all employees are focused 
on the same set of performance drivers, which are: 
Client Sales and Marketing (MAP1): This is about winning new business and retaining the Group's 
existing clients. The Group invests in sales and retention and is increasingly sectorising and sub -
sectorising its businesses around the world to allow it to get closer to clients. 
Consumer Sales and Marketing (MAP 2) : Like-for-like revenue consists of both volume and price, the 
Group is focused on attracting and satisfying its client base with strong consumer propositions.  
Cost of Food (MAP 3): Food makes up around one-third of the Group's costs. In addition to the benefits 
of its scale in food procurement, the Group aims to manage food costs through careful menu planning 
and by rationalising the number of products it buys. 
In-unit Costs (MAP 4): In-unit costs are made up predominantly of labour. By using labour scheduling 
techniques and improving productivity, the Group aims to deliver the optimum level of service in the 
most efficient way. 
Above-unit Overheads (MAP 5): The Group has a simple organisational model with few layers of 
management and little bureaucracy, which enables it to keep overheads low whilst it continues to  aim 
to grow revenue. 
The MAP framework has been highly successful in delivering and improving financial performance.
